results.title: South Korea vs. Czechia—World Cup: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
highlights:
The 2026 World Cup is finally here after what feels like an eternity of waiting, and next on the Group A fixture list following Thursday’s opener between Mexico and South Africa is a highly intriguing clash between South Korea and Czechia.
[...]
Czechia,
[...]
, where they edged past both the Republic of Ireland and Denmark on penalties—results that highlight their resilience and capacity to grind out results under pressure.
[...]
On paper, South Korea should win. It not only has the stronger qualifying record, but also greater star power than Czechia—most notably LAFC forward Son Heung-min and Paris Saint-Germain’s Lee Kang-in. It also brings far more experience on the big stage, having qualified for every World Cup since 1986, while Czechia returns to the tournament for the first time since 2006.
[...]
Czechia, meanwhile, under Miroslav Koubek, uses a similar structure but with a more attacking intent from the wingbacks, who are encouraged to get forward and deliver crosses into the box for tall center forwards.
[...]
Those contrasting approaches could cancel each other out, leading to a tight, tactical contest where clear chances are limited and a moment of quality, or a mistake, may decide the outcome.
[...]
South Korea ought to find that breakthrough, but it will not come easily—and Czechia will likely throw everything at it in the closing stages.
[...]

- Aerial threat: If Czechia is to trouble South Korea, it will likely come in the air. Its attacking options are all physically imposing, with several forwards standing well over six feet. Patrik Schick and Tomáš Chorý—at 6’3” and 6’6” respectively—pose a major aerial danger.
[...]
### Prediction: South Korea 1-0 Czechia
[...]
As mentioned, Czechia will likely look to play to its strengths, relying on attacking wingbacks who deliver crosses into the box for its physically dominant forwards.
[...]
That approach typically sees them line up in a 3-4-1-2 or 3-5-2 system, with David Jurásek on the left and Vladimír Coufal on the right, supporting a back three likely made up of Tomáš Holeš, Robin Hranáč and newly appointed captain Ladislav Krejčí.
[...]
In midfield, Tomáš Souček is expected to anchor the side alongside the experienced Vladimír Darida, with the pair providing both defensive protection and a significant aerial threat from deeper positions.
[...]
Up front, Patrik Schick is a guaranteed starter. If Czechia opts for 3-4-1-2, he will likely be partnered by Tomáš Chorý, with Pavel Šulc—the team’s creative maestro—operating as a No. 10. However, if it goes with an extra midfielder, Šulc will instead likely join the attack alongside Schick.

results.title: Czechia vs. South Korea Odds, Picks & Predictions - Group A, 06/11 - The Lines
highlights:
After all the hoopla and the run up, the 2026 World Cup gets underway with a Group A matchup as Czechia takes on South Korea Thursday night and we have you covered with our Czechia vs. South Korea prediction. Czechia ended up their tuneup for the World Cup by dropping Guatemala 3-1 in their previous match last Thursday. South Korea blanked El Salvador 1-0 in their final international friendly last Wednesday. This marks the first time that the two countries have met in World Cup play. Let’s break down this Czechia vs. South Korea matchup.
[...]
Czechia had their work cut out for them to just make the World Cup field. The Lokomotiva had to down Ireland and Denmark in shootouts in the playoffs to get here. Czechia comes in unbeaten in their last six matches dating back to last November. This marks the Lokomotiva’s 10th World Cup appearance but their first since 2006. They currently stand 41st in the FIFA rankings entering the World Cup. Czechia owns a record of 12 wins, five draws and 16 defeats. It might be tough sledding but they intend on making some noise in the tournament.
[...]
In their final tuneup ahead of World Cup action, Czechia took care of business against Guatemala. That allowed the Lokomotiva to head into play here with momentum. Patrik Schick opened the scoring and gave Czechia a 1-0 lead with his goal in the 11th minute. Pavel Sulc assisted on that marker. They gave up the tying goal in the 40th minute and the match was tied at halftime. After a flurry of substitutions for both sides, Tomás Chory gave Czechia a 2-1 lead. His goal, which came in the 72nd minute, was assisted by David Doudera. Denis Visinsky made it 3-1 and closed the scoring with his tally in the 79th minute of play. Matěj Kovář, who was 4-2-3 in World Cup qualifying, is the expected goalkeeper here. He finished with four clean sheets in those nine matches.
